antidotes.why: Peace follows at once from letting go of the fruit.

antidotes.source: Yoga Vasishtha 5.21.6; Narada to Shuka; Vidura
antidotes.why: Worry is fed by thought, so starve it with achintana to end worry.
Do not chase the future or brood on the past.
The child relies on the mother and stops worrying.
Freedom from anxious thought brings peace everywhere.

chains.summary: Dwelling on what is lost adds a second sorrow to the first. The medicine for sorrow is not to keep thinking of it. Thought about, sorrow does not leave, it grows. Meet the mind's pain with understanding and the body's with medicine.
chains.title: Not dwelling on it is the medicine

verses.m: When pain of body or mind arrives and nothing can be done about it, do not keep thinking about it. Not dwelling on it is the medicine for sorrow; brooding does not make it leave, it only makes it grow.
verses.sa: भैषज्यमेतद्दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत् / चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्धते दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते / यस्मिन्न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुचिन्तयेत्

verses.m: Heal the pain of the mind with wisdom and the pain of the body with medicine. That is what knowledge can do; don't behave like a child about it.
verses.sa: प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः / एतद्विज्ञानमसामर्थ्यं न बालैः समतामियात्

verses.m: No one should sit alone grieving over a trouble that has struck everyone. Instead of grieving, act to remedy it if you see a way.
verses.sa: न जानपदिकं दुःखमेकः शोचितुमर्हति / अशोचन्प्रतिकुर्वीत यदि पश्येदुपक्रमम्

chains.summary: Anger is the enemy hardest to defeat. Greed is the illness without end. The mind is faster than the wind. Worries outnumber the blades of grass.
chains.title: The enemy and the illness

verses.m: Yaksha: 'Which enemy is hardest to conquer? Which disease has no end? Who is considered good, and who is not?' Yudhishthira: 'Anger is the enemy hardest to conquer; greed is the disease without end; one who wants the good of all beings is good; one without compassion is not.'
verses.sa: कः शत्रुर्दुर्जयः पुंसां कश्चव्याधिरनन्तकः / कीदृशश्च स्मृतः साधुरसाधुः कीदृशः स्मृतः क्रोधः सुदुर्जयः शत्रुर्लोभोव्याधिरनन्तकः / सर्वभूतहितः साधुरसाधुर्निर्दयः स्मृतः

verses.m: Yaksha: 'What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? What is more numerous than blades of grass?' Yudhishthira: 'A mother is heavier than the earth; a father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; worries are more numerous than blades of grass.'
verses.sa: किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च स्वात् / किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात् माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात्पितोच्चतरस्तथा / मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्

chains.summary: Hope is a river whose water is wishes and whose waves are craving. Its crocodiles are attachment and its birds are restless thoughts. It uproots the tree of steadiness and its whirlpools are delusion. Its high banks are worry. Those who cross it with a clean mind rejoice.
chains.title: The river called Hope

verses.m: There is a river called Hope. Its water is wishes, its waves are craving; passions are its crocodiles, doubts its birds; it uproots the trees of courage; its whirlpools of delusion are hard to cross and deep, and its banks of worry tower high. Only great yogis, pure in mind, who reach the far shore, rejoice.
verses.sa: आशा नाम नदी मनोरथजला तृष्णातरङ्गाकुला रागग्राहवती वितर्कविहगा धैर्यद्रुमध्वंसिनी । मोहावर्तसुदुस्तरातिगहना प्रोत्तुङ्गचिन्तातटी तस्याः पारगता विशुद्धमनसो नन्दन्ति योगीश्वराः ॥

chains.summary: Craving leads a person like a bullock on a knotted rope and shrinks even the wise and brave to a blade of grass. Letting go of anxious thought is its cure.
chains.title: Craving on a rope

verses.m: Knotted inside the body and hard to cut, craving drags a person along the way a rope drags a bullock.
verses.sa: अन्तर्ग्रथितया देहे सर्वदुश्छेदयाऽनया । रज्ज्वेवाशु बलीवर्दस्तृष्णया वाह्यते जनः ॥

verses.m: People let go of all their sorrow when they let go of worry. Giving up worry is called the cure for the sickness of craving.
verses.sa: लोकोऽयमखिलं दुःखं चिन्तयोज्झितयोज्झति । तृष्णाविषूचिकामन्त्रश्चिन्तात्यागो हि कथ्यते ॥

verses.m: Even a man who is wise, brave and steady as Mount Meru, the best of men, craving alone turns into a blade of grass in an instant.
verses.sa: अपि मेरुसमं प्राज्ञमपि शूरमपि स्थिरम् । तृणीकरोति तृष्णैका निमेषेण नरोत्तमम् ॥

depicts.m: For one whose heart is scorched by the blazing sun of 'things I must do', where is happiness without the cooling rain of calm?
depicts.why: Depicts the endless list of obligations.

depicts.m: There is a river called Hope. Its water is wishes, its waves are craving; passions are its crocodiles, doubts its birds; it uproots the trees of courage; its whirlpools of delusion are hard to cross and deep, and its banks of worry tower high. Only great yogis, pure in mind, who reach the far shore, rejoice.
depicts.sa: आशा नाम नदी मनोरथजला तृष्णातरङ्गाकुला रागग्राहवती वितर्कविहगा धैर्यद्रुमध्वंसिनी । मोहावर्तसुदुस्तरातिगहना प्रोत्तुङ्गचिन्तातटी तस्याः पारगता विशुद्धमनसो नन्दन्ति योगीश्वराः ॥
depicts.why: Shows worry as the towering banks.

depicts.m: Yaksha: 'What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? What is more numerous than blades of grass?' Yudhishthira: 'A mother is heavier than the earth; a father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; worries are more numerous than blades of grass.'
depicts.sa: किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च स्वात् / किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात् माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात्पितोच्चतरस्तथा / मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्
depicts.why: Shows worries counted as more than blades of grass.

depicts.m: Dhritarashtra: 'Everything is always unsettled, and this mind is always unsettled. Wise one, tell me of the state that is free from unrest.' Vidura: 'I see no peace for you apart from learning and discipline, apart from mastering the senses, apart from giving up greed.'
depicts.sa: नित्योद्विग्नमिदं सर्वं नित्योद्विग्रमिदं मनः / यत्तत्पदमनुद्विग्नं तन्मे वद महामते नान्यत्र विद्यातपसो नान्यत्रेन्द्रियनिग्रहात् / नान्यत्र लोभसन्त्यागाच्छान्तिं पश्यामि तेऽनघ
depicts.why: Shows the king saying everything is always unsettled and this mind is always unsettled.

depicts.m: Remembering what she had done, her heart was full of a worry beyond telling. 'Shiva, an ocean of compassion, deep beyond measure, did not speak my fault aloud.'
depicts.sa: हृदयँ सोचु समुझत निज करनी। चिंता अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ कृपासिंधु सिव परम अगाधा। प्रगट न कहेउ मोर अपराधा ॥
depicts.why: Shows worry beyond telling as she goes over what she did.

depicts.m: Only one day of the appointed time, the support of his life, was left. Thinking of it, Bharat's grief was boundless. 'Why hasn't my Lord come? Has he forgotten me, knowing me to be crooked?'
depicts.sa: रहेउ एक दिन अवधि अधारा। समुझत मन दुख भयउ अपारा॥ कारन कवन नाथ नहिं आयउ। जानि कुटिल किधौं मोहि बिसरायउ ॥
depicts.why: Shows the mind supplying the worst reason for the silence.

depicts.r: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles, Fourth Series, CLVII, p. 494
depicts.sa: I have been living in mental hell. It is partially lifted now, and I hope for better days, better states.
depicts.why: Shows never a moment's peaceful life always high pressure.

depicts.m: The more you casually spin up fancies and possibilities, the more your world of troubles swells, through your own worrying.
depicts.sa: यथा यथा विकल्पौघान्संकल्पयसि हेलया । तथा तथैति स्फारत्वं संसारस्तव चिन्तया ॥
depicts.why: Depicts the spinning of scenario after scenario.

gloss: The mind runs ahead over what has not happened. The Yaksha is told worries outnumber blades of grass; the Manas calls worry a snake that has bitten everyone.

heals.m: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. From that renunciation, peace follows immediately.
heals.why: Names peace placed right after releasing the grip on results, not after mastering meditation.

heals.m: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
heals.sa: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
heals.why: The result was never in your hands; the work is.

heals.m: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
heals.sa: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
heals.why: Names success and failure held as one before the work begins.

heals.m: When pain of body or mind arrives and nothing can be done about it, do not keep thinking about it. Not dwelling on it is the medicine for sorrow; brooding does not make it leave, it only makes it grow.
heals.sa: भैषज्यमेतद्दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत् / चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्धते दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते / यस्मिन्न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुचिन्तयेत्
heals.why: Rumination is named as what feeds the pain.

heals.m: Brooding destroys beauty, brooding destroys strength, brooding destroys understanding, brooding brings on illness. Grief does not get you what you want; it only wears out the body and gladdens your enemies. Do not give your mind to grief.
heals.sa: सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते रूपं सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते बलम् / सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते ज्ञानं सन्तापाद्व्याधिमृच्छति अनवाप्यं च शोकेन शरीरं चोपतप्यते / अमित्राश्च प्रहृष्यन्ति मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः
heals.why: Counts what brooding takes: strength, judgement, health.

heals.m: And on top of that, I swear by Raghubir, I know no method of worship. A servant relies on his master, a child on its mother, and lives free of worry; the master has to look after him.
heals.sa: ता पर मैं रघुबीर दोहाई। जानउँ नहिं कछु भजन उपाई॥ सेवक सुत पति मातु भरोसें। रहइ असोच बनइ प्रभु पोसें ॥
heals.why: Gives the one relied on to do the looking after.

heals.m: He does not chase the future or brood on the past; he simply goes along with the present moment, smiling.
heals.sa: भविष्यं नानुसंधत्ते नातीतं चिन्तयत्यसौ । वर्तमाननिमेषं तु हसन्नेवानुवर्तते ॥
heals.why: Gives a picture of a mind not living ahead or behind.

heals.m: Worry grows by thinking, as fire grows with fuel; and it dies by not being thought, as fire dies without fuel.
heals.sa: चिन्तनेनैधते चिन्ता त्विन्धनेनेव पावकः । नश्यत्यचिन्ततेनैव विनेन्धनमिवानलः ॥
heals.why: Shows worry lives on the attention it is fed.

hero.m: Yaksha: 'What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? What is more numerous than blades of grass?' Yudhishthira: 'A mother is heavier than the earth; a father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; worries are more numerous than blades of grass.'
hero.sa: किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च स्वात् / किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात् माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात्पितोच्चतरस्तथा / मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्

loci.m: Whom has envy not stained? Whom has the wind of grief not shaken? Whom has the snake of worry not bitten? Who in the world has not been caught by illusion?
loci.sa: मच्छर काहि कलंक न लावा। काहि न सोक समीर डोलावा॥ चिंता साँपिनि को नहिं खाया। को जग जाहि न ब्यापी माया ॥

practices.m: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from the pure-hearted I accept.
practices.sa: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
practices.why: Shows devotion as what makes the gift.

practices.m: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
practices.sa: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥

practices.m: Ocean of compassion, Ganapati: may your radiance, which the whole world worships, by its own power quickly guard our minds, day and night, from wrong action, and urge them to good action. Blessed one, with Siddhi at your left side, we bow to you.
practices.sa: भर्गो विश्वसमर्चितं यदिह ते ह्यास्ते दयासागर ! तन्नो बुद्धिमहर्निशं गणपते ! शक्तचा स्वया सत्वरम । संरक्ष्यासत एव कर्मनिवहात् सत्कर्मणि प्रेरयेत् सियाऽलङ्कृतवामपार्श्व ! भगवस्त्वां सन्नमामो वयमा ॥

practices.m: Wish for what can be had, never for what cannot. Enjoy what is in front of you now, and do not grieve over what has not yet come.
practices.why: Shows enjoying what is present is named as the practice.

practices.m: Provisions for the wilderness of life, medicine that cuts the bonds of the world, rescue from sorrow and grief: the two syllables 'Ha-ri'.
Madhava is the father and the mother of all beings. Go to him for refuge, best of the Kurus; he is the refuge.
practices.sa: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पिता माता च माधवः / गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं शरण्यं कौरवर्षभाः

practices.m: Fair as the jasmine and the moon, beloved of Uma, home of compassion, who loves the lowly: may the destroyer of Kama show me grace.
practices.sa: कुंद इंदु सम देह उमा रमन करुना अयन। जाहि दीन पर नेह करउ कृपा मर्दन मयन ॥
practices.why: Shows an opening prayer for grace.

practices.m: Tulsi says: if you want light both inside and outside, place the name of Ram like a jewelled lamp on the threshold of your tongue.
practices.sa: राम नाम मनिदीप धरु जीह देहरीं द्वार। तुलसी भीतर बाहेरहुँ जौं चाहसि उजिआर ॥
practices.why: Shows the name kept at the threshold of the tongue.

stories.l: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.
stories.s: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
stories.t: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool

stories.l: You can make the best case for peace and still be refused. Speak anyway.
stories.s: Krishna travels to Hastinapura to plead for peace between the cousins. Elders, sages and finally Gandhari urge Duryodhana to share the kingdom; he refuses, even plotting to seize Krishna, and war becomes certain.
stories.t: Krishna's peace embassy to the Kauravas

stories.l: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.
stories.s: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.
stories.t: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting

stories.l: Helping is a privilege, not a debt someone owes you.
stories.s: The world does not need our help; helping is a privilege that makes us stronger. Expecting thanks brings unhappiness, so be grateful to the one you help. The world is a moral gymnasium, and calm people do the best work.
stories.t: Karma-Yoga 5: we help ourselves, not the world
